narrative.overview:
Daybook draws a calendar the way a network map draws a city. Each calendar is a line in its own colour, each event is a station dot on that line, an event that lasts a day or more is a horizontal line with rounded ends, and today is the interchange circle. The ground is one flat colour, midnight blue in the dark appearance and porcelain in the light one, and the two swap roles as ink. There is no brand accent: every hue on screen belongs to a calendar, and categories, which cut across calendars, are told apart by symbol, never by colour.

The system is dense and quiet. Month rows take the height of their fullest day, time-grid strips grow with their lanes, and no day ends in a count of hidden events. Type is the system face at Dynamic Type text styles with tabular figures; it condenses only when a column or a single word cannot fit, and at accessibility sizes the grids give way to full-width agenda rows. Structure comes from hairlines and one step of tonal depth between ground and rail. Controls, bars, sheets and menus are the platform's own (Liquid Glass on iOS 26 and macOS 26), tinted with ink.

This record describes the SwiftUI build on branch m5-search-polish (commit eea22db). Sizes are points at the default text size; most scale with Dynamic Type. In the frontmatter a `-dark` / `-light` suffix names the two appearances of one adaptive token, and `-ic` names its value under Increased Contrast. Evidence: iPhone and iPad portrait captures in `.impeccable/review/` from one build. The Mac has not been captured since milestone 1 and iPad landscape never; statements about them describe what the code does and are marked as not visually verified.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds, one ink each, swapped between appearances; no brand accent.
Calendar colour appears only as line (3 pt segment, 8 pt horizontal line, a coloured checkbox, a swatch) and as the tinted fill of a time-grid block.
One mark everywhere an event stands for itself: the station mark (month row, block, agenda, day sheet, detail, search).
Every event is on screen; rows grow, strips grow, views scroll.
System type, tabular figures, condensed width only when a column or a single word cannot fit.
Hairlines and one tonal step instead of shadows and cards.
Platform controls, platform motion, ink tint.

rules.name: The Line Is the Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Hue on a calendar surface means "this calendar" and nothing else. Selection, today, the current time, search matches, filter state and category identity are drawn in ink, weight or symbol. The only other hue is the platform's destructive and error red on delete actions and form errors.

rules.name: The Three to One Rule
rules.body: Every calendar line holds 3:1 against the ground in the appearance on screen, 4.5:1 under Increased Contrast, by lightness alone; hue never changes.

rules.name: The Own Hue Fill Rule
rules.body: A calendar colour used as a fill is mixed 22% into the ground in OKLab and given at least 0.045 chroma in the line's hue. Never transparency, never an sRGB mix, never full strength.

rules.name: The Passed Station Rule
rules.body: An event has passed when its end is at or before now (a zero-length event when its start is), and an all-day event when its last day is before today; an event in progress has not passed. It is drawn by hollowing the station (the ring and the line stay at full strength, the centre shows the surface behind it) and stepping the title to secondary ink, never by a hue, a grey wash or a veil over the cell. Passed blocks take an 11% fill with a 0.0225 chroma floor; a wholly passed span line is mixed 50% into the ground. That span line is the one stated exception to The Three to One Rule, and only outside Increased Contrast, where it stays at full strength.

rules.name: The Colour Plus Name Rule
rules.body: A calendar is never identified by colour alone: rail rows, picker rows, the detail's calendar row, day-sheet and search rows, and VoiceOver labels carry its title beside its colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that sits in a column uses tabular figures. In a month row the time is right-aligned in a slot as wide as "00:00", so titles share one left edge.

rules.name: The No Broken Words Rule
rules.body: Text never breaks inside a word. Rail names, add rows and block titles wrap between words; a title that cannot wrap holds one line with a tail ellipsis; a block's time shows as a range, then a start, then not at all; a place shows only if its first word fits.

rules.name: The Condense Only When a Word Cannot Fit Rule
rules.body: Grids condense as a whole below 130 pt columns. A wrapping name condenses only when its longest single word is wider than its column; otherwise it stays at standard width and wraps.

rules.name: The Weight Not Colour Rule
rules.body: Emphasis inside text, such as the matched letters of a search, is semibold, never a hue.

rules.name: The Nothing Hidden Rule
rules.body: A day shows every event of its enabled calendars and categories. Rows grow, strips grow, views scroll; no cell ends in "+3 more", a dot or a count. When a filter hides something, the shell says so.

rules.name: The Rows Before Columns Rule
rules.body: When columns cannot hold a title at the current text size, the layout becomes full-width rows. It does not shrink type and it does not drop events.

rules.name: The Title First Rule
rules.body: Where a bar must give way, the period title keeps its longest form first; controls take compact forms before the title shortens.

rules.name: The One Step Rule
rules.body: There are two surface levels, ground and rail. A new surface is one of them; it does not introduce a third tone, a gradient or a shadow.

dos: Do draw calendar colour only as line, checkbox, swatch or the Own Hue Fill, always through the line adjustment for the ground on screen.
Do mark selection, today, the current time, search matches and filter state in ink, weight or symbol.
Do use the station mark wherever a row stands for one event.
Do put new list sheets on the rail colour with rows in the ground colour; reading surfaces (the detail) go on the ground.
Do write every time through `TimeText`, and set aligned figures tabular.
Do give new rail rows the shared trailing column, a 44 pt target and names that wrap between words.
Do provide the agenda fallback for any new grid at accessibility sizes.
Do give every adaptive colour an Increased Contrast value, and check text on a block against 4.5:1 and any new preset against 3:1 on both grounds.
Do build new metrics as scaled metrics tied to a text style.
Do mark an event that has passed by hollowing its station and stepping its title to secondary ink.
donts: Don't hide events behind a count, a dot or a "more" link in any view.
Don't give the interface a hue of its own; a blue control or highlight reads as a calendar line.
Don't give categories colours; they are told apart by symbol.
Don't fill with a calendar colour at full strength, by opacity, or by an sRGB mix.
Don't grey out, veil or recolour past days or events, and don't add a now line to the month.
Don't add shadows, gradients or a third surface tone.
Don't round the end of a span line where the event continues.
Don't let text break inside a word, or condense text that would fit by wrapping.
Don't let category symbols take room from a title.
Don't replace the navigator, the station mark or the interchange circle with system pickers or badges that bring their own accent.
